title: Machine learning helps identify 61 new cataclysmic variables in SDSS-V spectroscopy
summary: A convolutional neural network shortlisted cataclysmic-variable candidates from more than two million SDSS-V spectra, reducing the spectra requiring visual inspection to about 2% of the total. Human review and follow-up analysis of the resulting 504-object sample reported 61 previously unreported cataclysmic variables, spectroscopically confirmed 248 candidates and yielded 82 new or improved orbital periods; the article discusses selection biases and the CNN missed 27 spectra later found by human review.
ai_technology: Convolutional neural network classifier for SDSS-V/BOSS spectra
organization: SDSS-V collaboration; University of Warwick and collaborating institutions

evidence.tested: A convolutional neural network shortlisted cataclysmic-variable candidates from more than two million SDSS-V spectra, reducing the spectra requiring visual inspection to about 2% of the total.
evidence.unknown: This is one grouped paper-level survey result, not 61 separate records. The CNN was a triage aid rather than an autonomous confirmation system; authors report completeness/selection limitations and 27 misclassified spectra discovered through human inspection.
evidence.ai_role: Ranked over two million spectra for likely cataclysmic variables, reducing the manual-inspection workload; human investigators visually inspected candidate spectra and established source classifications and periods.
